name: nds_backup
statement: The cartridge's backup memory (the save chip) on the auxiliary SPI bus: AUXSPICNT (0x040001A0) puts the slot in serial mode (bit 13) and keeps the chip selected while bit 6 holds; each byte written to AUXSPIDATA (0x040001A2) is one transfer and the chip's answer reads there afterwards. A serial flash answers READ, FAST READ, RDSR, RDID, WREN/WRDI, PAGE WRITE, PAGE PROGRAM, PAGE ERASE and SECTOR ERASE. Which chip a game has is data here (by game code, without the region letter): the cartridge header does not say.
table_note: by_game_code as numbers for the card language: per game, its code's first three letters (the first in the lowest byte), the kind's number and the size in bytes

flash_commands.0x0A: PAGE WRITE (3 address bytes, data within a 256-byte page)
flash_commands.0x02: PAGE PROGRAM (bits only go from 1 to 0)

registers.name: AUXSPICNT
registers.bits: 0-1 baud rate, 6 hold chip select, 7 busy (never shown: transfers finish at once), 13 serial mode, 14 ROM transfer IRQ, 15 slot enable

limits: serial flash only (no EEPROM or FRAM chips, no infrared cartridges); program and erase finish at once (status never shows busy); a game missing from the table gets the default chip
sources: GBATEK (DS cartridge backup: SPI bus, flash commands)
